title: Hēra: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens

body:
# Hēra: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Hēra** stay *hera*.

Hēra's myths are almost all variations on one theme: the wronged wife defending her throne. She cannot overthrow Zeús, but she can punish his lovers and their children with relentless ingenuity. Zeús and Hēra were married in a sacred ceremony on the island of Samos, one of her great cult centers.  Their wedding night lasted three hundred years, according to one tradition, establishing the pattern of divine marriage.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Hēra
- **ASCII form:** hera
- **Meaning:** "Lady, mistress (possibly related to ἥρως)"
- **Domain of influence:** Marriage, Women, Queen of Gods
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἥρα
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 102 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἥρα**. On the evidence, it means "Lady, mistress (possibly related to ἥρως)".

Strip **Hēra** to *hera* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **e → ē** — Eta: long epsilon: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Hēra** lives at [/sites/hera/](/sites/hera/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/hera/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/hera/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/hera/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Hēra** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Wedding, Family & Maternity** — Marriage itself; the queen who sanctifies the union.
- **Women's Health & Femtech** — Marriage and childbirth were her household; the whole arc of women's lives ran under her eye.
- **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** — Queen of gods; sovereignty’s other half.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/hera/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Hēphaistos** ([read it here](/sites/hephaistos/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Hēraklēs** ([read it here](/sites/herakles/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
